title: VibeGraph project envelope IR
description:
Project-mode wrapper around per-file IRs (schemas/ir.schema.json). Adds project-scoped fields the v2 thread-organisation work depends on. See PLAN-v2.md §1.1.

M8.1 baseline: envelope ships with empty `entryPoints` and `threads` arrays. M8.2 fills `entryPoints` (auto + manual). M8.3 fills `threads` by running extract_thread.py over each entry point at parse time.

M19.1 (PLAN-v5 §1.1): bumped 2.0 -> 2.1 by ADDING the `system` field — a pure roll-up of the already-parsed threads + effectKind + entryPoints into subsystems + cross-subsystem edges (scripts/build_system_tier.py). Additive only: no per-file IR change, no enum change. The system tier is language-shallow (LIGHT path, PLAN-v5 §0.3) — the frontend is one node, detected by convention + a text scan, never parsed.

Versioning is independent of the per-file IR. Adding envelope-level fields bumps to 2.x additively; removing or changing existing fields is a 3.0 break.

version.description: Project envelope schema version. v2.0 = M8.1 baseline; v2.1 = M19.1 adds `system`; v2.2 = M-LANG1 (multi-language seam: per-file IRs may carry a `language` discriminator, and EntryPoint.framework is an open string — the closed Python-framework enum would have failed validation for every non-Python frontend). The server continues to emit 2.1 until a non-Python frontend is registered; both loosenings are additive, so 2.1 envelopes validate unchanged.

files.description: Map of project-relative file path -> per-file IR (schemas/ir.schema.json). Validated structurally as object-of-objects here; per-file schema validation is the IR snapshot test's job (test:ir). v2.2 (M-LANG1): each per-file IR may carry a `language` discriminator (python|bash|jsts|cpp), server-stamped on v1.x IRs and frontend-emitted at IR 2.0; absence means python.

symbolIndex.description: Project-wide flattened symbol index — union of every per-file IR's symbolIndex. Each entry self-identifies its source file via the `source` field. Empty until populated; M8.1 emits the union of per-file entries.

entryPoints.description: Detected and manual thread entry points. Empty array in M8.1; populated in M8.2 by scripts/discover_entry_points.py.

threads.description: Threads extracted at parse time, one per entry point. Empty array in M8.1; populated in M8.3 by running scripts/extract_thread.py over each entryPoints[] item.

system.description: M19.1 (PLAN-v5 §1): the system tier — a pure roll-up of threads + effectKind + entryPoints into subsystems and the cross-subsystem edges between them. Emitted by scripts/build_system_tier.py. Derivation only; no new parsing. The system view (M19.2+) renders this.

systemPlan.description: PLAN-v7 Stage 3 (additive, OPTIONAL — no version bump; envelopes without it validate unchanged): the ratified architecture PLAN, when one exists. A LABELLED PLAN traceable to the user's description, NEVER honest IR — a SIBLING of `system`, composed with it only at render (planned subsystems ghost-render; ids that exist in the honest tier are already real). Persisted at <projectRoot>/.vibegraph/system-plan.json on human acceptance; becomes honest only when built code re-parses into matching subsystems.

workRun.description: M-AGENT1 (additive, OPTIONAL — no version bump; run-less envelopes validate unchanged): the Agent Manager's durable run — task → plan_work packets → per-packet status/evidence, persisted at <projectRoot>/.vibegraph/work-run.json on every transition. Two human gates are STRUCTURAL (draft→ratified and awaiting-review→done are transitions only a human message triggers); the orchestrator automates between them. Inner shape pinned by src/server/work_run.ts + test/work_run.test.mjs; validated structurally here.

buildPlan.description: PLAN-v7 Stage 5 (additive, OPTIONAL — no version bump): the ratified BUILD PLAN (the roadmap) + its live per-item status. A LABELLED PLAN and the orchestrator's durable state: persisted at <projectRoot>/.vibegraph/build-plan.json on ratification and re-persisted on every status transition, so a run survives reloads and resumes from disk. The human gate stays at every increment — the orchestrator automates BETWEEN gates, never through them.

constraints.description: M-CONTRACT.3 (additive, OPTIONAL — no version bump): the STATED constraints (.vibegraph/constraints.json) the server attaches to a live envelope, when any exist. Declared here at M-STACK.1, which added the sibling below — `additionalProperties: false` had made a live constrained envelope fail validation. Inner shape pinned by src/server/constraint_store.ts; validated structurally here.

crossings.description: M-XLANG.1 (additive, OPTIONAL - no version bump; crossing-less envelopes validate unchanged): where a logic thread LEAVES its own language over HTTP, and which route in this project serves the path it calls. Derived from parsed data on both sides - the caller's URL argument reduced to a static path shape, and the receiver's route metadata from any language's discoverer (src/server/crossings.ts). WEIGHED, never resolved: `confidence` is path+method only when BOTH sides parsed a method, `ambiguous` names every candidate and claims none, `unmatched` means the path resolved but nothing here serves it, and `note` always says what the match could not establish. A crossing does NOT widen the thread - `threads[].filesReached` stays one language.

stack.description: M-STACK.1 (additive, OPTIONAL — no version bump; stack-less envelopes validate unchanged): the STACK FACTS — which software tools the project uses, each with its role, origin, declared version (manifests only), the project funnel that wraps it, and the parse EVIDENCE behind it. Pure derivation from `files` + `threads` + the manifests on disk (src/server/stack.ts), rebuilt on every derived refresh and never persisted. A tool the taxonomy does not know is listed with role "unknown" — the spec names what it cannot classify. A stated DECISION about a tool is not here: that is a constraint of kind "stack-policy".

byThreadCalled.description: M-BOUNDARY.2 (additive, OPTIONAL): entry point -> the tools a BOUNDARY of that thread actually reaches, as opposed to `byThread`, which is the tools PRESENT in the files it walks. Present is a superset of called; the difference is a dead dependency or a resolution gap, and both views are rendered so neither can be mistaken for the other. Absent when the index was built without thread nodes.

localsByFile.description: M-RESOLVE (additive, OPTIONAL): per file, the local names its ASSIGNMENTS bind and what each was bound from (`valueKind`, plus `callTarget` when it was a call). A third of every unresolved receiver in the real fixtures is bound to a literal three lines up - `problems = []` above `problems.push` - so this is what makes that class free to resolve, with no run and no model. A name bound twice with different shapes is refused rather than guessed.

importsByFile.description: M-BOUNDARY.1 (additive, OPTIONAL): per file, the local names its imports bind and the specifier each came from, so a call's receiver head can be resolved to a tool by the server, the contract and the webview through one shared function (src/shared/stack_attribution.ts). `project` marks a specifier that resolves INSIDE this project - a call through it is project code, never a tool.

Crossing.description: M-XLANG.1: one hop out of a thread's language or process. `kind` (M-FLOW.2, additive; absent = http): `http` — `path` is the static shape the caller's URL yields (`*` is an interpolated segment) and `targets` the routes that serve it; `command` — `path` is the string literal naming a script this project parses and a target's `route` is that parsed file; `tool` — `path` is an MCP tool name and the targets its registrations. Every candidate when ambiguous.

StackTool.description: M-STACK.1: one software tool the project uses. `role` is the closed taxonomy set (src/shared/stack_taxonomy.ts); `origin` third-party / stdlib / project (a project module that funnels a tool — the proxy case — carries `wraps`). `evidence` is the parse sites that prove it: import / call / include, or `config` for a manifest-only fact (the M-LANG3 limit: .js/.jsx are not parsed, so for an unparsed web frontend the manifest is the only fact and is labelled as such).

roleSource.description: M-CMD.2 (additive, OPTIONAL): absent = a taxonomy table classified this tool; "stated" = a stack-policy in .vibegraph/constraints.json named it with a role because no table could.

roleStatedBy.description: M-CMD.2: the id of the constraint that stated the role.

roleStatedSource.description: M-CMD.3 (additive, OPTIONAL): that constraint's source. "agent" = a model's classification from the classify pass, NOT human-reviewed; a human's statement outranks it.

home.description: M-BOUNDARY.1: origin "project" only - the file that IS the funnel. Its importers are listed in `files` too and sit BESIDE it, not inside it, which is the difference between a call that goes THROUGH the wrapper and one that merely lives in a file importing it.

calledOn.description: M-BOUNDARY.2 (additive, OPTIONAL): the threads with a BOUNDARY attributed to this tool - a subset of `threads`, which is file-level presence.

BuildPlan.description: PLAN-v7 Stage 5: an ordered, dependency-aware capability list decomposing the ratified SystemPlan. Foundation-first is STRUCTURAL: an item's needs[] may only reference ids declared BEFORE it (build order = declared order), making the graph a DAG by construction. groundedIn quotes the user's description or is null = INFERRED.

SystemPlan.description: PLAN-v7 Stage 3: a proposed architecture. Deliberately NOT $defs/Subsystem or $defs/SystemEdge — those carry parse-derived facts (endpointRefs, refs, confidence, evidence) a plan cannot honestly claim. Instead every planned item carries GROUNDING: `groundedIn` quotes (or closely paraphrases) the user's description; null = INFERRED (proposed unasked) and the gate renders that distinction.

description.description: The user's project description this plan traces to. Non-empty.

drafted.description: True when `claude -p` drafted the plan (Stage 3b); false for canned/user-authored proposals.

ratifiedAt.description: ISO timestamp of human acceptance. Present once persisted.

System.description: Subsystems and the cross-subsystem edges between them (PLAN-v5 §1.1).

SubsystemKind.description: Closed set for v5 (PLAN-v5 §1.2). fs/subprocess/log effects are deliberately NOT subsystems (§5.4).

Subsystem.description: One architectural node. `id` grammar: bare kind (`frontend`/`backend`/`db`/`cache`/`library`) or `external_http:<host>` (one node per distinct host). Edge endpoints reference these ids, optionally endpoint-qualified as `<owner>:<entryPointId>` for backend/library origins.

framework.description: Backend/frontend framework discriminator (e.g. 'flask', 'React'). Null when not meaningful.

threadRefs.description: PLAN-v5 5.3 (additive, OPTIONAL): every thread that TOUCHES this subsystem, by entryPointId - not only the ones whose entry point it owns. A thread belongs to as many subsystems as it reaches: an ingest route is a backend thread that also writes the db and posts a webhook. Derived from the effect edges' existing viaThread handles, so it needs no new evidence; absent when no thread reaches this card.

endpointRefs.description: Backend and library: the entryPoints[].id values the card owns — for backend, kind=route only (the M19.2 expand-to-reveal endpoints; effect edges may originate from non-route backend entry points too, not listed here); for library (M-NN-2), the routeless project's own non-manual entries (model/public_api/cli/test).

fileCount.description: Backend and library (when the card owns entry points): number of project (.py) files.

detectedBy.description: Frontend only: how the convention scan flagged it (e.g. 'package.json:react + 2 component file(s)'). No JS was parsed.

path.description: Frontend only: project-relative directory of the frontend source.

evidence.description: Derived subsystems (db/cache/external_http): why this node exists (e.g. 'effectKind:db', 'name-match').

SystemEdge.description: A cross-subsystem edge. `effect` edges (confidence=high) roll up an effectKind/name-match hit reached inside a thread; `viaThread` is the drill-down handle into threads[]. `calls` edges (confidence=low) are frontend->endpoint route-string text matches — the only language-crossing, and it is text not AST.

from.description: Source subsystem id, possibly endpoint-qualified (`backend:<entryPointId>` / `library:<entryPointId>`) for effect edges, or the bare `frontend` for calls edges.

to.description: Target subsystem id (`db` / `cache` / `external_http:<host>`) for effect edges, or `backend:<routeEntryPointId>` for calls edges.

confidence.description: high = derived from parsed effectKind; low = heuristic (frontend string-scan).

evidence.description: How the edge was derived: 'effectKind' | 'name-match' (cache) | 'string-scan' (frontend calls).

effectKind.description: System-tier effect classification (effect edges only). DISTINCT from the per-file IR EffectKind enum — `cache` is classified at the aggregation layer by name-match, not in the per-file IR (PLAN-v5 §6, Q6).

viaThread.description: effect edges: entryPoints[].id of the thread this edge was rolled up from — the drill-down back-pointer. Null for library origins with no entry point.

refs.description: Source sites backing this edge, as '<relpath>:<line>' strings.

EntryPointKind.description: How this entry point was discovered. See PLAN-v2.md §1.2 for per-kind detection rules. `model` = a PyTorch nn.Module subclass's forward() method (the model's data path) — surfaced so ML projects aren't blank in the thread launchpad.

EntryPoint.description: A function (and the file it lives in) flagged as a thread seed. `id` is the join key into threads[].entryPointId.

id.description: Stable per-entry-point id, formatted '<file>:<funcName>'. Used as threads[].entryPointId back-reference.

file.description: Project-relative path of the file containing the entry-point function.

irNodeId.description: Structural-path id of the function in the per-file IR.

label.description: Display label — usually the bare function name.

summary.description: One-line summary derived from the function's docstring (or signature, if no docstring). Optional in M8.1; M8.3 fills.

framework.description: Framework discriminator for kind=route / kind=cli / kind=model detections. Null for kinds where framework is not meaningful. Well-known Python values: 'argparse', 'click', 'typer', 'flask', 'fastapi', 'django', 'pytest', 'pytorch' (`pytorch` added with M-NN-2's library_only fixture — discover_entry_points.py had emitted it on kind=model since the Arch-view arc, but no committed envelope carried a model entry until then). v2.2 (M-LANG1) OPENED this from a closed enum to a free string: each language frontend's discover step names its own frameworks (e.g. 'shell', 'express', 'fastify') — a closed list here would fail envelope validation for every non-Python frontend.

metadata.description: Kind-specific extras — e.g. { 'route': '/users/<id>', 'method': 'GET' } for routes, { 'decorator': '@app.cli.command' } for CLI. Free-form object; consumers must check kind first.

ProjectThread.description: A thread (extract_thread.py output, version 1.0) plus envelope-level back-references and computed reach-set. Inner shape unchanged from src/webview/threads/types.ts:Thread.

version.description: Inner thread shape version — pinned by extract_thread.py output.

entryPointId.description: Back-reference into entryPoints[].id. Null for ad-hoc seeds that weren't promoted to entry points.

filesReached.description: Computed: every project-relative file path the thread touches (DFS over thread nodes' .file). Drives §1.5 unreachable-file filtering in the thread view.
